archetypes.name: background-migration-parity
archetypes.rationale: Diff flips many foreground blocks to immediate-background across design and implement SKILL.md; parity gaps and leftover foreground directives are high-impact orchestration risks.
archetypes.prompt_body: Audit the staged diff for a complete, consistent foreground-to-immediate-background migration across skills/design/SKILL.md and skills/implement/SKILL.md. Flag any remaining contradictory foreground-required callouts, missing run_in_background or timeout annotations on long-running fenced Bash blocks, and scripts named in the plan (review loop, ship-pr, other >=30s helpers) that the diff still leaves foreground-only. Compare analogous steps between design and implement for mismatched wait semantics or anti-halt prose that could cause turn-ending halts after background completion. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: timeout-tier-calibration
archetypes.rationale: The diff introduces multiple distinct timeout values (600000, 1800000, 21600000) without mechanical enforcement; mis-tiered timeouts can truncate long loops or mask hung jobs.
archetypes.prompt_body: Review every new immediate-background timeout in the diff and classify each fenced script by expected wall-clock class (summary/publish, checks, multi-hour review or ship loops). Check that scripts with similar runtime profiles use consistent timeout tiers within and across design versus implement SKILL.md, and that the chosen values plausibly cover worst-case round caps without being so short they abort normal runs. Flag scripts where timeout is absent, duplicated inconsistently, or orders of magnitude off relative to sibling steps. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: background-resume-state
archetypes.rationale: Backgrounding review and ship drivers changes orchestrator turn boundaries while mid-loop resume contracts (--starting-round, ship-pr-state.sh, step-5-resume) must stay coherent.
archetypes.prompt_body: Trace how switching run-step5-review.sh, design-step3-review.sh, step-8-ship.sh, and related helpers to immediate-background mode interacts with documented resume, persist or rollback, and continuation envelopes in the diff. Look for architectural breaks where a background return could skip task-notification handling, re-enter a loop at the wrong phase, lose round or state-file updates, or conflict with NEVER rules forbidding polling or ScheduleWakeup. Pay special attention to main-agent handoff branches (MAV, coder-main-agent-required, per-round approval) that assume a single completion boundary. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.
